## How to Contribute

First, you need to fork the repository to your GitHub account. This creates a copy of the project under your account.

- Go to the [ImageEditor repository](https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor).
- Click the "Fork" button at the top-right corner of the page.

### 2. Clone Your Fork

Next, clone the forked repository to your local machine to start working on your changes.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/your-username/ImageEditor.git
cd ImageEditor
```

### 3. Create a Branch
Create a new branch for your changes. It's important to use a descriptive branch name to indicate what you are working on.
```sh
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

### 4. Make Your Chamges
Now, you can start making changes to the project. Whether it's fixing a bug, adding a new feature, or improving documentation, ensure your changes are clear and concise.
- Follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines.
- Write clear and descriptive commit messages.
- Test your changes thoroughly.

### 5. Commit Your Changes
Once you are satisfied with your changes, commit them to your branch. Make sure your commit messages are descriptive.
```sh
git add .
git commit -m "Add a detailed description of your changes"
```

### 6. Push to Your Fork
Push your changes to your forked repository on GitHub.
```sh
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
```

### 7. Open a Pull Request
Now, you are ready to open a pull request (PR) to the main repository.
- Go to the original [ImageEditor repository](https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor).
- Click on the "Pull Requests" tab.
- Click the "New Pull Request" button.
- Select your branch from your forked repository and compare it with the main repository.
- Fill out the PR template with a clear and detailed description of your changes.
- Submit the pull request.

### 8. Address Feedback
Once your pull request is submitted, it will be reviewed by project maintainers. You may be asked to make some changes. Be responsive to feedback and make the necessary updates.

## Reporting Bugs

If you find a bug, please report it by [creating an issue](https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor/issues) in our GitHub repository. Please include:

- A clear and descriptive title.
- A detailed description of the bug, how to reproduce it, and what you expected to happen.
- Any relevant screenshots, code snippets, or error messages.

## Suggesting Enhancements

We welcome suggestions to make ImageEditor better! To suggest an enhancement:

- Open an issue on GitHub with a clear and descriptive title.
- Provide a detailed description of the enhancement, why it would be useful, and how you envision it working.

## Your First Code Contribution

If you're new to contributing to open-source projects, here are some ways you can start contributing to ImageEditor:

- Fixing typos or improving documentation.
- Addressing open issues.
- Adding new features or improving existing ones.

Please check our list of [good first issues](https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A"good+first+issue") for ideas.

## Pull Requests

When you're ready to contribute code, please follow these steps:

1. Fork the repository to your GitHub account.
2. Clone the forked repository to your local machine:
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor.git
   ```
3. Create a new branch for your changes:
```sh
git checkout -b your-feature-branch
```
4. Make your changes and commit them with clear and descriptive commit messages.
5. Push your changes to your forked repository:
```sh
git push origin your-feature-branch
```
6. Open a pull request in the main repository:
- Go to the original repository and click on the "Pull Requests" tab.
- Click on the "New Pull Request" button and follow the prompts to create your pull request.

## Code Style

To maintain a consistent codebase, please adhere to the following coding standards:
- Use appropriate naming conventions for variables, functions, and classes.
- Ensure your code is well-commented and easy to understand.
- Follow the formatting guidelines for C++ (e.g., proper indentation, spacing).

## Code of Conduct
This project adheres to the [Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TitikshaBansal/ImageEditor/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By participating, you are expected to uphold this code. Please report unacceptable behavior to [titikshabansal0209@gmail.com](mailto:titikshabansal0209@gmail.com).

## Thank You!
Thank you for taking the time to read through these guidelines and for contributing to ImageEditor. Your contributions are what make this project successful and impactful. We look forward to working with you!
